comments.author: @RyanCart96
comments.text:
Great video. Just one small linguistic request: could you consider using 'the US' or 'the (United) States' rather than 'America' when referring specifically to the country? The name _America_ originally referred to a much broader geographical region, encompassing lands far beyond the present-day US. Over time, the US effectively co-opted the name in English, despite being just one of many countries in (the) America(s). For millions of people, particularly in Latin America, _América_ refers to their continent too, so using it exclusively for the US can feel rather exclusionary. Especially in geopolitical analysis, I think the more precise terminology would be welcome. 

With regards to the demonym: As someone from the US, I prefer to refer to myself as a Usonian, but I do realise that's not quite caught on just yet. 😅
